keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 800-1469. Redrawn after review (the first draft used the whole Amazonas department, 138 cells, 66 of them north of 5°S in the Jivaroan lowlands, which the page does not give the Chachapoya). The page: 'the southern part of the Department of Amazonas'; the territory 'encompassed the triangular region formed by the confluence of the Marañón River and the Utcubamba in Bagua Province, up to the basin of the Abiseo River where the Gran Pajáten is located' and 'land to the south up to the Chuntayaku River, exceeding the limits of the current Amazonas Region towards the south'; 'the center of the Chachapoya culture, though, was the basin of the Utcubamba River'. Drawn as Amazonas within 110 km of Chachapoyas (60 cells, about 15,200 km2, which reaches the Bagua triangle and stops short of Condorcanqui) plus a 75 km disc at Gran Pajatén (7.649 S 77.418 W, the Gran Pajatén page; San Martín, between the Marañón and Huallaga) for the Abiseo basin and the southward extension; the two pieces touch (121 cells, about 30,600 km2). Area check: the page has no km2 figure; Garcilaso's 50 by 20 leagues is about 31,000 km2 (my conversion, 1 league about 5.55 km) against 30,500 km2 drawn, ratio 0.99. The Chuntayaku River is not in the gazetteer and the page does not place it, so the disc's southern edge (about 8.3 S) is a reading, not a limit; the Abiseo basin has no gazetteer entry (disc used).

wars.name: Chachapoya rebellion against Huayna Capac
wars.outcome: Governors and ministers were killed; Huayna Capac attacked and crossed the Marañón on rafts; women at Cajamarquilla asked for mercy and the Inca granted peace.
wars.note: Undated on the page (placed in Huayna Capac's reign 1493-1527); after the culture's drawn end. No border moved.

certainty.note: No limits on the page; the redrawn pieces stand for river basins (Utcubamba, Abiseo) and a southward extension that no page bounds.

sources.title: Chachapoya culture
sources.note: c. 800 to the Inca conquest about 1470 (also 'around 1475'); Utcubamba basin; Kuélap and Gran Pajatén; rebellion under Huayna Capac; 1547 Spanish. sources.title: Kuélap
sources.note: Built in the 6th century, most structures 900-1100, 6 ha, 3,000 inhabitants, abandoned 1570.

sources.title: Gran Pajatén
sources.note: Coordinates 7°38′56″S 77°25′05″W, San Martín Region on the border with La Libertad, between the Marañón and Huallaga; the page does not describe an Abiseo basin (Abiseo is the national park's name); attributed to the Chachapoya mainly on architectural evidence.

notes: Typed 'culture': the pages describe chiefdoms and fortified towns (Kuélap, Gran Pajatén), no state; identity.capitals is empty because neither page calls a site the capital (Kuélap page: no capital). The Chachapoya page dates the conquest 'about 1470' in the overview and 'around 1475' later; Kuélap page gives no Inca date and says Kuélap 'was abandoned in 1570 due to the Spanish Conquest'. Gran Pajatén and Kuélap 'likely defended against the Wari culture around 800 AD'. San Martín is not named by the page. The Inca Empire dossier carries the matching gain at 1470. The List of wars involving the Inca Empire page dates the conquest of the Chachapoyas to 1472 (Inca victory); the culture page's 'about 1470' is kept. Review fix (2026-10-19): the extent was the whole Amazonas department; it is now the southern Amazonas (110 km round Chachapoyas) plus a 75 km disc at Gran Pajatén for the Abiseo basin, the same region in the ledger, the war zone and the Inca successor land. San Martín is still not named by the Chachapoya page; the Gran Pajatén page places the site in San Martín, and the Gran Pajatén page says the visible ruins date from Inca times (occupation from 200 BCE), so the Chachapoya attribution of that site rests on architecture; the Chachapoya page's own sentence is what draws the Abiseo basin.
